categories.main_business_segments: Tokyo Tatemono operates four main business segments: (1) Building Business, which includes the development, sale, leasing, and management of office buildings, commercial facilities, and logistics centers; (2) Residential Business, focused on the development, sale, leasing, and management of condominiums and other housing; (3) Asset Service Business, which covers real estate brokerage, consulting, and parking lot operations; and (4) Other Businesses, including quality-of-life services (hotels, spas, golf courses), asset management, and overseas real estate development.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages expertise in large-scale urban redevelopment, sustainable building design (including ZEB/ZEH standards), and integrated property management. It utilizes advanced project management for complex, mixed-use developments and incorporates renewable energy solutions and green building certifications in its logistics and office properties. Digital marketing and web-based sales support are also used in residential sales.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include corporate tenants (for office and commercial buildings), individual homebuyers (for condominiums), institutional investors (for asset sales), and end-users of parking, hotel, and leisure facilities. The company serves a broad range of industries, with a particular focus on urban business districts, residential buyers in metropolitan areas, and investors seeking real estate assets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Tokyo Tatemono's core operations are in Japan, especially the Tokyo metropolitan area and other major cities (Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka, etc.), but it also has an expanding presence in overseas markets such as the United States, Australia, Thailand, and China through subsidiaries and affiliates.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily as a downstream player, acting as a developer, owner, and operator of real estate assets, as well as a service provider in property management, brokerage, and asset management. It also engages in upstream activities through land acquisition and project planning for development.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include accelerating asset turnover, strengthening stable income bases, and enhancing capital efficiency. The company emphasizes sustainable urban development, decarbonization (CO2 reduction targets), digital transformation, and diversity & inclusion in human capital. Overseas expansion and large-scale redevelopment projects are key growth drivers, with a focus on innovation in green building and community value creation.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through property sales (condominiums, buildings, and investment assets), rental income from owned properties, property management and brokerage fees, parking lot operations, and service fees from hotels, leisure, and asset management. The business model combines recurring income from leasing and services with transactional income from asset sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Japanese real estate developers such as Mitsui Fudosan, Mitsubishi Estate, Sumitomo Realty & Development, and Nomura Real Estate. Tokyo Tatemono is positioned as a leading integrated developer with strengths in both large-scale urban redevelopment and residential development, but is smaller in scale than the largest industry players.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending December 2024, consolidated operating revenue was 463.7 billion yen, with operating profit of 79.7 billion yen and net income attributable to parent company shareholders of 65.9 billion yen. The company has shown strong growth, with revenue up 23% and net income up 46% year-on-year, and total assets exceeding 2 trillion yen. The company targets further profit and capital efficiency improvements through its mid-term plan.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tokyo Tatemono differentiates itself through its expertise in large-scale, high-value urban redevelopment, commitment to sustainability (including decarbonization and green building), and integrated service offerings across the real estate value chain. The company emphasizes creating both 'place value' and 'experience value' for communities and customers, and aims to balance social value creation with corporate growth.
